svg.title: Pilot and wire coefficient bounds use one output cube before L is chosen. The mass filter costs C decayj(l) with positive principal lower bound; rails have common upper and positive principal lower bounds. At nonzero aliases Dl,a and R−1 cost respectively C grade(l)−2 and C grade(l)−4; the l seed representation bounds S. The inverse-alias bounds use the common-collar reciprocal argument and the bulb and bend bounds. The sums H, Ta contain two smoothing factors, contributing decay2j, while each D contributes another inverse grade squared. Each resulting weight is bounded above by decay2 for j ≥4, whose uniform finite-alias sum pays both sums. The quantity U = |m(q0)|2 P a fa + SH is bounded above and has a positive real lower bound from its principal filter and one fa, all summands being nonnegative. The common-collar lemma bounds U−1 and hence the source rests, fled and gains in fixed orientation dimension.
